purpose: Bounded native-function tool-selection comparison: AgentCPM first pair, Qwen four-case sequence, and Fara text-only first pair, on clarified BART research, explicit-confirmation, unresolved-city, and stale-feedback decisions.
scope: AgentCPM ran the first two prepared cases only; Qwen ran those same two plus unresolved-city and stale-action heldouts. This compares an off-source native-function interface bundle, not the production JSON-schema interface: no browser/MCP dispatch or effects occurred, and no model or native-function adapter was promoted. A separate local prerequisite-stage production planner change is recorded in the linked archive below. The loaded-page missing-city path is reachable; the controlled actual-host characterization below shows that specific path failing its city gate. The earlier counterfactual capture alone did not prove that failure. A subsequent controlled actual-host loaded-page characterization is now recorded below; it does not change the off-source status of the native-function comparisons. A Fara two-case text-only native-function compatibility run is recorded below; it did not exercise Fara screenshot/browser protocol, MCP dispatch, or application effects.

decisions: UI-TARS remains experimental; no automatic model/routing change.

semanticSummary.clarifiedCase: Useful openLink choice: l10 is the official BART discounts result, with every requirement still pending. No dispatch was enabled.
semanticSummary.explicitConfirmationCase: Fails the explicit gate: openLink l13 selects the youth application result before asking permission, despite the user condition. No dispatch was enabled.
semanticSummary.interpretation: Across the AgentCPM first pair and Qwen four-case sequence, relevant ordinary navigation and stale-feedback choices are useful; AgentCPM misses the explicit confirmation gate, while Qwen honors it. Qwen chooses openLink despite unresolved city in a counterfactual loaded-page case whose untrusted captured page/URL remains San Francisco-specific. This is interface-bundle evidence, not a pure schema-format A/B or proof of a production missing-city failure. The actual-host characterization below independently confirms this specific loaded-page path fails its city gate, without establishing that every loaded-page workflow fails. These comparisons did not change the model or native-function interface; no adapter/model was promoted. The separate local prerequisite-stage planner change is recorded below. Fara produced the expected scoped calls on both first-pair cases: openLink l10 for the observed official BART result and askUser before opening a result for the explicit condition. The second question is awkward/presuppositional and ends with a stray quote; only the call-order condition matches. This text-only interface probe does not qualify Fara browser execution, visual capability, or whole-task performance.
semanticSummary.managedLoadedPage: Actual default HostComputerUseManager/production browser-loader characterization with an already-loaded seeded page failed the missing-city gate: the planner assumed San Francisco from page context and asked permission to follow a page link. The goal contract also misclassified official-source-link inclusion as an action. The test had two planner calls and no navigation beyond the seed; this establishes failure for this controlled path only.

semanticReview.loadedPageDecision: The page-step proposal asked approval to follow the seeded “Youth fare details” link, even though the user had requested an official source. It assumed San Francisco BART from the page and did not ask which city the user meant.

semanticReview.effects: No navigation beyond the seeded page and no visual model launch. The proposed link was not dispatched.
